changes: Notifications use existing apiJson instead of three independent cookie-only fetch paths. Lists validate rendering-relevant fields; writes share one function that requires success plus a list of affected IDs, with bounded waiting and no automatic write replay.

The backend mark-all and clear-all routes share a handler, retaining authenticated user ownership, marked count and the existing durable-save barrier. Receipts additionally identify all affected notifications, allowing the client to reconcile exactly what the server processed.

AppContext merges both notification actions into one confirmed operation. It retains state on failure, serializes clicks, disables both panel actions while waiting, and suppresses stale reads and old-account write completions.

Local notifications present at the click and server-confirmed affected IDs form the update set. New local or unaffected notifications arriving while the request is in flight survive. New clear operations no longer write a local timestamp that hides unconfirmed server data.

Account switches now clear the previous notification list and cancel the pending write, sharing the existing auth generation. Existing legacy clear boundaries are still read for compatibility. The inaccurate promise of an unimplemented later retry was deleted.
AppContext reuses the existing NotificationItem type instead of a duplicate interface. NotificationCenter renders both actions together and calculates its unread count once.

PersonalityEditor reuses useApiCollection for authenticated reads, cancellation, response validation and retry. A failed or pending configuration no longer blocks the Contacts tab. Account/work-domain/organization changes remount owned configuration state.

Deleted duplicate personality loading headers, duplicate cognitive/social vector renderers, and the hand-maintained seven-section expansion map and click callbacks. Native details/summary controls preserve the original three initially expanded sections; evolution receives the actual loaded personality ID.
validationNotes: Four added UI/context behavior cases (including a parameterized mark/clear case) cover HTTP and incomplete-receipt failures, no premature local change, duplicate-click suppression, newly arrived notifications, obsolete reads, account changes, cancellation, credentials, contacts availability during personality failure, retry, native fold interaction, malformed config and scope isolation.
Notification route integration assertions now check affected IDs and that clearing one user preserves another user. The auth recovery fixture was extended with notification request ownership refs.

AppContext and the notification service execute against synthetic fetch. PersonalityEditor and ContactsPanel are mounted; only the separately covered evolution child is replaced in that test. Backend routes use an isolated test database.

All focused tests, lint including TypeScript, all-frontend and desktop builds, compact-layout checks and the direct backend build passed. No capability documentation was regenerated. All prune40-68 latest file baselines matched.
limitations: Notification ownership remains per user as in the existing backend, not separate per organization. The operation gate is per AppProvider; it is not a multi-window transaction or a new backend rollback mechanism.

Canceling the frontend cannot undo a write already accepted by the server. Unconfirmed writes leave client state intact and allow explicit retry; no automatic later retry is promised. A storage failure can still leave the existing backend mutation pending, as reported by sendDurableMutation.

New notification clients require the updated backend ID receipt. Old clients can ignore the added field; pairing a new client with an old backend intentionally yields an unconfirmed-operation error rather than assuming success.
Legacy notification clear boundaries remain readable. No existing user preference, notification, model credential or case record was changed by this work.

Native personality disclosure state is per mounted panel and resets to its initial sections after a tab unmount or account/scope switch. Validation covers rendering-critical fields, not the full domain schema or live evolution refresh of every displayed field.

No full-suite run, production backend/API calls, native client acceptance, commit, push, deployment or client restart. Completion of this batch does not mean the entire repository has completed final simplification and acceptance.
